review: The hymn is personal testimony in the first person: 1:1–4 is 1 Pet 3:15 with Song 5:16, 2:1–4 is Gal 2:20 with Ps 38:5, 3:1–4 is Ps 103:3 with Ps 139:5, 4:1–4 is Ps 94:19 with Eph 3:19, and 5:1–4 is Ps 23:4 with Prov 18:24.

The refrain זֶה דּוֹדִי, הוֹי הֲמוֹנִים closes every stanza exactly as the print repeats ذَا حَبِيبِي يَا جُمُوع; the payload does not vary it, because the hymn's form is the public repetition of a private claim.
1:2 צְלָעַי — the Arabic بَيْنَ الضُّلُوع is 'between the ribs'; the Hebrew uses צְלָעוֹת, the word of Gen 2:21 and Exod 26:20, so the love is lodged in the body's frame and not merely in feeling.
